g.text: A crusty, chewy sourdough bread with robust flavor and rich golden color, made entirely with
sourdough starter for leavening. Requires minimal effort with no kneading, just folding and a long
cold fermentation, resulting in a stunning, delicious loaf.
1. In a large mixing bowl or 6-quart food-safe plastic bucket, combine the sourdough starter,
water, bread flour, salt, and diastatic malt powder (if using).
2. Mix and stir everything together to make a sticky, rough dough. If using a stand mixer, beat
at medium speed with the paddle attachment for 30 to 60 seconds; if not, stir with a large spoon
or dough whisk until everything is combined.
3. Cover the bucket or bowl with a lid or plastic wrap and let the dough rise for 1 hour.
4. Gently pick up the dough and fold it over on itself several times, cover it again, and let it
5. Repeat the rising-folding process one more time (for a total of 3 hours), folding after the
last hour. Then place the bucket or bowl in the refrigerator and let the dough rest for at least
6. Turn the dough out onto a well-floured work surface and shape it into a rough ball. Leave the
dough seam-side up, cover it, and let it rest on a floured surface for 15 minutes.
7. Shape the dough to fit your baking vessel: a 13" log for a 13" pain de mie pan or long
covered baker, or a large round boule for a round baker or Dutch oven. Lightly grease the inside
of your baker, dust the inside with semolina, or place the dough on a sheet of parchment. Place
the shaped dough in the baker (along with parchment if using) and cover it with the lid.
8. Let the loaf warm to room temperature and rise for about 2 1/2 to 3 hours. The loaf will
